name: mean_reversion_hull_ma_5s
author: adapted from Gemini Quant
thesis: Exploits the lag-less nature of Hull Moving Average (HMA). When price deviates too far from the 50-bar HMA and the HMA slope is flat, a reversion is imminent. Behavioral bias: traders see the price moving away and chase it, creating the extreme deviation required for the snap-back.
mechanism: Short-term selling exhausts available demand at a price level, creating a temporary liquidity vacuum. Market makers who absorbed the selling begin marking prices back to reduce inventory risk. Limit buy orders resting below create a floor, and new participants entering the long side accelerate the reversion as the forced selling pressure dissipates.
weaknesses: Requires high volatility to hit 1% deviation
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; apply to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index instead of FnO universe; stop/target recalibration for 5-second timeframe. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
